data.content_ref: inline:Emit, in the same pass as the fixed point, a minimal witness subgraph for every committed label: for a refuted node, the accepted attacker chain; for an accepted node, the absence of any accepted attacker within the extension; for a suspended node, the vacuous empty witness. Witness choice uses a deterministic tie-break so the whole computation stays a pure function of the graph and each witness is bounded by edge count, preserving polynomial cost. The criticizable point: minimal-witness selection may require a global minimization that breaks locality and cannot be computed incrementally, and vacuous witnesses for suspended nodes invite a false reading that suspension is evidenced when it is precisely the absence of a decision.
